text: Vietnam, China strengthen cooperation in water resource management and disaster prevention
Vietnam and China are expanding their exchange of hydrological data, collaborating on training, and applying technology in water resource management and disaster prevention.

Vietnamese Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Environment Nguyen Hoang Hiep met with Chinsese Deputy Minister of Water Resources Liu Dongshun and his delegation in Hanoi on November 17. during their visit to Vietnam to attend the second Mekong-Lancang Water Resources Cooperation Ministerial Conference.
During the meeting, Deputy Minister Nguyen Hoang Hiep assessed that water resource management, irrigation, and disaster prevention are effective areas of cooperation between the two ministries.
Recent exchanges of meteorological and hydrological information have supported forecasting, water resource management, and disaster prevention efforts.
Ensuring water security and information sharing is a crucial aspect of cooperation, both in bilateral relations and within the Mekong-Lancang framework, the Vietnamese deputy minister noted.
He acknowledged the cooperation of the Chinese Ministry of Water Resources in installing water level and rainfall measurement stations and exchanging data.
He noted that the automatic information sharing mechanism, with a frequency of four times a day, is practically significant for forecasting, especially long-term forecasts.
Based on this, Vietnam wishes to expand the number of stations, supplement data, and enhance real-time information sharing capabilities.
Timely exchange of reservoir operation information also helps specialized agencies be more proactive in managing water resources, responding to floods, droughts, and saltwater intrusion.
In addition to data, the Vietnamese deputy minister also called for more cooperation in human resource training and the application of science and technology.
He expressed a desire for China to offer scholarships in the field of irrigation and facilitate the exchange of lecturers and students between educational institutions of the two countries.
The Deputy Minister also proposed cooperation in research, training, and technology transfer, especially in artificial intelligence, automation, and digital transformation in irrigation.
These are areas where Vietnam is keen to learn from experience to manage, operate infrastructure systems, and use water resources efficiently.

With many transboundary rivers, maintaining information sharing between the two countries is essential, he said, adding that information from both upstream and downstream will support proactive management and risk prevention efforts.
Chinese Deputy Minister Liu Dongshun, for his part, agreed on the need for information exchange in disaster prevention and mitigation.
He emphasized that with many transboundary rivers, maintaining information sharing between the two countries is necessary.
Information from both upstream and downstream will support proactive management and risk prevention efforts.

Deputy Minister Liu Dongshun also welcomed proposals on human resource training and advanced technology research, while introducing China's experience in flood and drought prevention, water-saving practices, and protecting river and lake ecosystems.
Regarding future cooperation, he proposed that the two ministries consider signing a Memorandum of Understanding on cooperation in water resources.

Specialized agencies, research institutes, universities, and enterprises from both countries can expand technical exchanges on dam safety, river mouth management, delta management, digital twin technology application, and developing water sector technical standards.

During the meeting, both sides also discussed effectively implementing the minutes of the online meeting on August 11, 2026 (signed on November 16, 2026, during the visit) regarding the emergency meteorological and hydrological data sharing mechanism between China and Vietnam.
